fichas.title: Shed Construction: Principles and Performance
fichas.summary: Industrial production and warehouse buildings are often designed as single-storey sheds with large spans and generous room heights. Construction may use timber, steel or reinforced concrete. Shed layouts are shaped by machinery, access routes and vehicle turning circles. Advantages include economical lightweight roofs, natural lighting, heavy floor loading and a one-level flow of people and materials; disadvantages include high land use and unfavourable thermal behaviour. Rooflights, northlights and light domes can provide lighting and ventilation.

fichas.title: Structural Systems for Industrial Sheds
fichas.summary: The page illustrates single-span and multi-span shed systems, including cable-trussed, trussed and web-girder beams; tension-braced and cable structures; space frames; laminated-timber portal forms; fixed-joint and two-hinge frames; and pond roofs with fixed-end columns. Multi-span arrangements may be added, staggered or formed with continuous beams. Shed height and loads may depend on the proposed overhead crane.

fichas.title: Shed Roof Forms for Lighting and Ventilation
fichas.summary: Illustrated roof configurations include laminated-timber sheds with ridge rooflights, transverse light bands, vaulted northlight roofs, cantilever shells with skylights, vertical sawtooth glazing, self-supporting northlight roofs and northlight roofs with cross-bracing in the glazing. The text notes that lighting, ventilation and smoke extraction can be provided by roof light bands, northlights or light domes, with strip windows also possible in the façade.
